sampling.rule: one block in every 6-hour UTC slot since 2023-01-01, at a seeded random moment inside the slot

culprits.method: NEAR RPC chunk {block_id, shard_id} for each sampled block with a shard over 50%; accounts ranked by receipts + transactions received

predictions.author: Headroom (github.com/london160771/headroom)
predictions.rules: Frozen. This file is never edited after it is committed. Its SHA-256 is in predictions/SHA256 and in the git tag predictions-v1, and predictions/predictions.json.ots is an OpenTimestamps proof that anchors that hash in Bitcoin. Each prediction is scored by lib/predictions.js on every build, from sampled mainnet blocks inside its window. Thresholds are shares of capacity (0 to 1).

predictions.text: NEAR's gas price stays at the floor in at least 99% of sampled blocks.
predictions.if_wrong: Blockspace is getting scarce. The bear reading (fees can't rise from demand) is wrong.

predictions.text: No calendar month averages more than 20% of NEAR's gas capacity.
predictions.if_wrong: Demand has returned to the March 2024 peak or beyond, with 10 shards instead of 4.

predictions.text: In every month, the hottest shard in a block stays under 50% of its limit at the 95th percentile.
predictions.if_wrong: If P1 still holds, NEAR has a hot-shard problem its fee rule can't see, and congestion control is doing the work.

predictions.text: No sampled block crosses NEAR's 50% fee trigger (gas used summed over all chunks vs the summed limit).
predictions.if_wrong: Whole blocks are filling. The fee multiple is not a far-off number any more.

predictions.text: Gas burn offsets less than 5% of the new NEAR minted over the window.
predictions.if_wrong: Usage is starting to pay for security. Burn is becoming a real sink, which is bullish for the token.

predictions.text: In June 2027, NEAR uses less than 5% of its gas capacity.
predictions.if_wrong: Load grew about 9x or more in seven months. The headroom is being used up faster than the thesis says.
